dimension: Portfolio Renewal Pricing on Post-1995 / Costa-Hawkins-Exempt Units
verified_practice_summary: Public multifamily REITs AvalonBay (AVB) and Equity Residential (EQR) (~184k homes) reported 2Q26 renewal Like-Term Effective Rent Change of 4.1% (accelerating to 4.8% in July 2026) vs. 0.8%–2.0% on new move-ins; SF/NorCal same-store market rates rose 6.5%–7.3%.
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Corporate renewal averages (4.1%–4.8%) come from newer Costa-Hawkins-exempt luxury complexes and CANNOT be applied to a 1940 SF rent-controlled duplex capped at 1.6%.

dimension: SF Rent-Controlled Assets & Automated Annual Cadence
verified_practice_summary: Institutional operators track exact unit anniversaries in property-management ERPs, upload bulk Excel Housing Inventory filings (>=5 units template) on portal.sfrb.org before March 1, and issue routine annual AGA increases every 12 months rather than banking for 6+ years.
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Adopt the corporate compliance habit: file Housing Inventory before March 1 each year and apply predictable, modest annual AGA adjustments on the exact anniversary date rather than jarring multi-year catch-ups.

dimension: Formal Passthrough Petitions (Capital Improvement / Bond / O&M)
verified_practice_summary: Large SF landlords use dedicated legal/accounting teams to file Rent Board Capital Improvement Petitions (amortized 7–20 years), G.O. Bond Worksheets, and Water Bond Passthroughs prior to serving passthrough notices.
verified_value: Advance Rent Board certification mandatory before passthrough
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Never fold property-tax, insurance, or renovation costs into base rent informally; use separate Rent Board passthrough forms and exclude passthroughs from base rent.

dimension: Algorithmic Revenue-Management Software Prohibition in SF
verified_practice_summary: U.S. DOJ & State of California sued RealPage and major corporate operators (Case No. 1:24-cv-00710) over algorithmic renewal alignment; San Francisco enacted Ord. 224-24 (SF Admin Code § 37.10C, eff. Oct 14, 2024) banning algorithmic rent-setting devices citywide.
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Do NOT use algorithmic pricing tools or competitor nonpublic rent feeds to justify or set residential rents in San Francisco.

verified_practice_summary: California Attorney General guidance and enforcement warn against unlawful fee unbundling, electronic-only rent mandates (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.3 requires at least one non-cash/non-electronic payment option), and email/text rent notices.
verified_value: Paper/check payment option & written mail/personal notice mandatory
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Continue accepting standard check/non-electronic payment options and never impose new utility/admin surcharges outside the Rent Ordinance.
official_source_label: CA Dept. of Justice (Attorney General) — Tenant Rights

verified_practice_summary: SF Rent Board June 10, 2025 Commission Minutes record Executive Director Varner reporting that outreach across 123,356 Housing Inventory filings (108,534 licenses issued) showed many SF landlords had not raised rents for years while others served increases without realizing a license was required.
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Unit 2's unchanged $3,150 rent since 2019 is common among individual SF owners, but banking catch-ups fail immediately if the owner skipped Housing Inventory licensing.

dimension: Good-Faith / Tax & Insurance Hardship No Defense to Procedural Defect (Outer Sunset Case)
verified_practice_summary: In Appeal AL260003 (2395 – 47th Avenue, Outer Sunset, Feb 10, 2026), an ALJ ordered the landlord to refund $14,742.04 in unlawful rent increases (Aug 2022 – Jan 2026); the Commission voted 5–0 to deny the landlord's appeal despite claims of good faith and property-tax/insurance burden.
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Even in the exact same Outer Sunset neighborhood, good faith and rising taxes/insurance will NOT save an unlicensed or procedurally defective rent increase.
official_source_label: SF Rent Board Commission Minutes (Feb 10 2026 PDF)

verified_practice_summary: In Appeal AL250027 (7115 Geary Blvd, June 10, 2025), the Commission voted 4–0 that a landlord's Costa-Hawkins increase was unlawful because an original occupant still resided there and a tenant CANNOT waive Rent Ordinance lawful-rent rights even by prior settlement.
verified_value: Waiver of Rent Ordinance rent cap void (AL250027)
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Never ask Unit 1 (Tenant 1A & Tenant 1D) or Unit 2 to sign an informal 'voluntary' side agreement exceeding the Rent Ordinance cap — it is void and refundable at any time.
official_source_label: SF Rent Board Commission Minutes (June 10 2025 PDF)

dimension: Citywide Average Actual Rent Increase % Imposed by Owner Size
verified_practice_summary: No official government agency publishes a verified SF-specific statistical mean/median comparing actual percentage increases imposed by corporate REITs vs. individual 2–4 unit owners on rent-controlled units.
compliance_takeaway_for_94122_owner: Left blank and flagged unverified per strict zero-inference policy; rely on statutory 1.6% cap and documented SEC/Rent Board records rather than unverified industry anecdotes.
